title: MULTI-STEP PROCESSES
subtitle: A business action spans several services and any step can fail halfway. Make progress durable and failures reversible.
footer: Theory: DDIA ch 9 Consistency and consensus · DDIA ch 11 Stream processing · DDIA ch 12 The future of data systems

items: One user action touches several services or external APIs: booking + payment + confirmation, ride lifecycle, order fulfilment.
Steps can take seconds to days, or depend on outside callbacks.
A business action spans several services, and no distributed ACID transaction is available.
Any step can fail after earlier steps succeeded.
A saga runs a compensating action for each completed step (refund, release, cancel), in reverse order.
A durable orchestrator records progress after each step, so a crash resumes where it stopped instead of starting over or forgetting.
Is there a cross-service transaction? Replace it with a saga: a compensating action for each step.
Who drives the steps? An orchestrator (Temporal, Step Functions) is easier to reason about than event choreography for complex flows.
Are all steps idempotent so retries are safe?
Do events leave the database reliably? Use the outbox pattern.
What happens on timeouts with unknown outcomes? Query status; don't blindly retry side effects.

blocks.text: "There is no distributed transaction across booking and payment, so I'll run a saga: hold the room, charge, confirm, and if the charge fails, release the hold. A workflow engine persists progress so a crash resumes instead of restarting."

items: Non-idempotent steps that double-charge on retry.
Dual writes to a database and a queue without an outbox.

blocks.text: Used in: Payment system (Stripe), Online judge (LeetCode), Job scheduler
